label: Late original phase / <DEL> when the sequence starts with digit 3
explanation: Fires on original-phase steps t>=3 and on the <DEL> step of sequences whose first (or second) original token is the digit 3. The core case, first token = 3, is near-deterministic: 99% precision, holding 59% of activation mass and 93% of the top activation quartile. Every top example starts with 3, often a run of 3s. Activation builds over steps 3-6 and peaks shortly before or at <DEL>. It then decays quickly over the first one or two copy steps, which output the leading 3s, and is essentially silent for the rest of the copy phase and at t<3. Adding orig(1)==3 brings in weaker activations. A first token of q or v produces weaker, less reliable firing. The remaining roughly 20% of mass is diffuse low-magnitude firing late in the original phase of other sequences, more often when digits are present, with no clean token rule.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the first original token (most: 3, q, v, p, x, 2; least: a, 0, n, w) and the second original token (most: 3, q, v, x, c, p; least: n, a, w, 0); timing cues that raise it most: t=5, t=4, t=6.
